evidence.source: Ministry of Education, R.O.C., Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A02475 爻: Mandarin Pinyin and character explanation
evidence.text: The record gives 爻 the current Mandarin reading yáo (語音), with xiáo as a separate reading variant. It also says that 孝 and 教 have a left upper part derived from 爻, whose form changes in that position. This supports a graphic relationship, not by itself a phonetic analysis of 教.
evidence.title: 教育部《異體字字典》: 爻

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, R.O.C., Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A01726 教: transmitted Shuowen form and Mandarin readings
evidence.text: The record gives 教 the current Mandarin readings jiào and jiāo, with separate senses: jiào includes instruct/guide and causative uses; jiāo means impart or teach. It quotes the transmitted Shuowen form 敎 as composed of 攴 and 𡥉. This lexicographic account does not independently establish the early phonetic role of 爻.
evidence.title: 教育部《異體字字典》: 教

search_audit.outcome: One search followed by opening both exact requested Taiwan MOE records. 爻 lists yáo (and xiáo as a separate reading); 教 lists jiào and jiāo. The 教 entry quotes Shuowen's 敎 composition from 攴 and 𡥉; the 爻 entry describes a graphic derivation in the left portion of 孝/教.

gaps: Local kMandarin rows were checked internally: neither sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt nor pipeline/data/unihan-kmandarin-hsk1.tsv has a kMandarin row for 爻 or 教. The full local Unihan file contains an unrelated U+31710 kFanqie row matching the text string 教, not a reading row. No local rows are emitted as external evidence.
The MOE's graphic derivation statement does not verify 爻 as the phonetic component in early 教; it is used here only to document the stated graphic relationship.
